analysis:
CHANGELOG.md units 12 and 13 (head text, lines 865+ and 1314+) are documentation only. They describe the profiler, runtime manifest, release candidates and earlier releases. I found no executable change and no change to the trust assumptions in the threat model. Unit e5cc14cefb263fc0:0 carries only metadata for coordinator/api/consumer.go (mode 100644, unchanged), and nothing in it is a security change.

coordinator/api/consumer.go patch (e5cc14cefb263fc0:1) changes first-content deadline handling in two ways.
- In the quick-capacity preflight path (around line 797), ttftThreshold is now recomputed per candidate as max(1ns, time.Until(query.FirstContentDeadline)). It becomes 0 when the deadline is zero.
- In the chat handler (around lines 2308-2376) and the generic endpoint handler (around lines 2888-2937), a new deadlineForWork closure is built from s.promptWorkDeadlineForRequest. It is passed through inferenceAdmissionParams.deadlineForWork and reapplied after model fallback using promptwork.FromContext.

These changes affect only routing, deadline and availability behavior. They touch no auth, billing, encryption, attestation or App Attest authorization (TB-011/T-053/T-054) logic, and they do not change prompt plaintext handling (T-003). I saw no new data exposure or plaintext sink.

Limits on this pass: the bodies of promptWorkDeadlineForRequest and runInferenceAdmission, and the use of the new deadlineForWork field, are not in the supplied patch. A later pass should confirm that a zero or expired deadline fails closed to a retryable 429 rather than disabling the TTFT gate or leaving reservations unreleased (refundReservation paths, A-009). I made no finding because nothing visible shows a concrete security regression.
